subject: SLO deviation: automatic routing fallback triggered for hosted API (p95 spike)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simone Alvarez <simone@brightgate.com>, ops@brightgate.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLO deviation: automatic routing fallback triggered for hosted API (p95 spike)

Hi Simone / BrightGate ops team,

Quick heads up — at ~08:45 PST today our monitoring detected a sustained p95 response-time spike for your production traffic routed to our hosted inference cluster in us-west-1. To protect interactive latency SLAs we automatically triggered a gated routing fallback to a lower-latency variant (reduced batch sizes + quantized model) and moved a subset of traffic to a secondary pool. You may have seen an increase in partial or slightly lower-quality generations for ~14 minutes while the fallback was active.

What we observed
- p95 increased from ~420ms to ~1.2s for requests with average sequence length of 450 tokens.
- error rate remained within thresholds (no 5xx spike).
- automatic fallback routed ~27% of BrightGate traffic to backup pool between 08:46–09:00 PST.

Immediate customer impact
- Transiently higher latency for some requests; a small fraction of responses showed truncation / slightly more concise outputs during fallback.

What we did
1) Automated routing fallback to lower-latency variant for 27% of traffic.
2) Scoped and rotated affected worker nodes to restore normal kernel scheduling.
3) Telemetry capture and snapshot attached (incident_snapshot-20270108.json) plus p95 graphs.

Next steps
- We are doing a detailed post-incident analysis and will post a concise incident summary to status.redwoodinference.com (link in email) within 24 hours.
- I will coordinate a short tech-review with your SREs if useful — propose 30-minute window today at 16:00 PST.

Apologies for the disruption. We prioritized latency SLO protection and reverted traffic to standard routing at 09:00 PST once kernel contention subsided.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SLO deviation: automatic routing fallback triggered for hosted API (p95 spike)

Simone — quick answers while we triage deeper:
- No implicit retries were performed by Redwood. All customer requests were forwarded (no silent retries). We only adjusted routing / model variant.
- Attached snapshot includes request IDs binned by latency; I pulled two example request IDs that hit the fallback and showed shorter outputs: req-20270108-78a2 and req-20270108-9c4f. We redacted payloads but included timing and token counts.

Root cause hypothesis (initial)
- We observed kernel-level scheduling contention on a subset of GPU workers after a background maintenance job interacted poorly with our continuous batching heuristics for longer contexts. That amplified p95 for long tokens sequences.

Immediate mitigation applied
1) Traffic gated to lower-batch path + fallback model variant (quantized).
2) Evicted and cycled the handful of affected worker nodes.
3) Tightened a batching timeout threshold to avoid similar amplification during jobs.

Follow-ups planned
- Postmortem with timeline and permanent fix by EOD tomorrow.
- We will produce a signed SLA credit calc if you prefer — happy to discuss.

Karthik
Director, Inference Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: SLO deviation: automatic routing fallback triggered for hosted API (p95 spike)

Hi Simone — thanks for joining the brief sync earlier. Quick post-call summary and links you asked for: 

Summary
- Window: 08:46–09:00 PST on 2027-01-08.
- Impact: Elevated p95 for some long-context requests; ~27% of traffic served via fallback model variant for 14 minutes.
- User-visible: Slight increase in latency and a handful of shorter outputs for long requests. No increased 5xx rate.

What we’ve delivered
- Full incident snapshot (attached).
- Public incident page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/2027-01-08-hosted-p95-spike (will be updated with postmortem tomorrow).
- Permanent fixes planned: improved batch-timeout heuristics, stronger isolation for maintenance jobs, and a canary gating change for quantized variants.

Next steps for BrightGate
- We offered an optional SLA credit; if you’d like that calculated, reply with the account contact for billing.
- If you want a joint tech review of the postmortem, we can schedule next week.

Again — apologies for the disruption. We’ll send the full postmortem and remediation timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
